key_insight: Code2Video uses AI-authored 3D proxies to guide video structure and motion. The reported findings suggest that more detail is not always better: coarse proxies favor natural motion, while the best proxy design depends on the task.
problem_solved: How should 3D proxies and prompts be designed to improve generated videos while balancing explicit control and natural-looking motion?
method: Use agent-authored 3D proxies as structural and dynamic guides for video generation.
Run controlled experiments varying proxy granularity, physics simulation, and prompting.
Compare results through blinded human evaluation to identify task-dependent trade-offs.
impact: For practitioners, proxy complexity is a design choice rather than an automatic quality upgrade. The supplied abstract is truncated, so conclusions about medium-granularity proxies and other settings cannot be confirmed.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: AI agent → 3D proxy → guided video generation.
Side-by-side coarse and medium proxy examples illustrating different levels of detail.
Conceptual balance graphic showing structural control versus natural motion.
Evaluation schematic showing blinded reviewers comparing generated clips.
paper_title: Coda-DaVinci: Reimagining Video Generation with Code2Video
paper_authors: Yiyan Ji, Qixun Wang, Yang Shi, Zhuoran Zhang, Yifan Xu
